item.text: {"question_id":"2B.1","answer":"During 2023, Tshisekedi used formal diplomatic and executive-security channels to pursue alternatives to force, including Nairobi and Luanda processes, ceasefire and M23-withdrawal mechanisms, regional-force coordination, MONUSCO cooperation, and proposed cantonment, disarmament, and P-DDRCS pathways (BATCH-0021-E001; BATCH-0021-E003; BATCH-0027-E010; BATCH-0027-E013; BATCH-0008-E009). He also convened a national round table involving government officials, legislators, senators, and provincial representatives to review whether the state of siege should be maintained, requalified, or lifted, and called the P-DDRCS a peaceful exit for armed groups (BATCH-0007-E002; BATCH-0007-E003). However, the record does not show that these processes were consistently inclusive or effective. The EAC political track excluded M23 after Kinshasa rejected dialogue with it, and the government adopted a hardline position while regional diplomatic and military efforts produced no measurable security improvement according to one scholarly assessment (BATCH-0011-E017). Ceasefire arrangements reduced hostilities for several months but broke down in October, after which M23-related violence increased and the FARDC’s cooperation with non-state armed groups created escalation risks (BATCH-0027-E006). The coercive state-of-siege framework was repeatedly extended—over 50 times according to Amnesty—without meaningful public debate, while civilian administration and elected provincial assemblies were displaced; presidential extension measures were formally recorded in July 2023 (BATCH-0012-R03-E001; BATCH-0012-R03-E003; BATCH-0015-E007). Thus, the evidence supports substantial formal diplomacy and some peaceful alternatives, but also exclusionary dialogue policy, continued coercive mobilization, weak legislative/public deliberation on the state of siege, and limited verified implementation. Whether more credible alternatives were feasible, and whether Tshisekedi authorized force only after exhausting them, remains uncertain.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0021-E001","BATCH-0021-E003","BATCH-0027-E010","BATCH-0027-E013","BATCH-0008-E009","BATCH-0007-E002","BATCH-0007-E003"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0011-E017","BATCH-0027-E006","BATCH-0012-R03-E001","BATCH-0012-R03-E003","BATCH-0015-E007","BATCH-0007-E013"],"limitations_and_gaps":["The supplied evidence does not provide complete cabinet, parliamentary, or classified deliberations concerning particular force decisions.","Several favorable items document announced plans, commitments, or coordination mechanisms rather than verified implementation, funding, compliance, or outcomes.","The evidence does not establish a definitive counterfactual about which peaceful alternatives were feasible or whether all credible options were exhausted before force was authorized or supported.","The adverse account of rejecting dialogue and the hardline stance includes reported interpretations and attributed claims, while external actors, M23, Rwanda, and regional mandate disputes also materially shaped the available choices.","The repeated state-of-siege extensions are relevant to formal process and coercive security governance but are not, by themselves, proof of a specific international-force decision. "],"corrections_made":["Qualified the claim that Tshisekedi simply rejected political dialogue by specifying that the EAC political track excluded M23 after Kinshasa rejected dialogue with it, while preserving the evidence of regional diplomacy.","Added the omitted state-of-siege evidence, distinguishing formal presidential extensions from the reported absence of meaningful public debate and the displacement of civilian institutions.","Removed or qualified unsupported implications about the sincerity of negotiations and causal responsibility for failed ceasefires or military stalemate.","Specified that several positive records establish formal plans and commitments, not completed implementation or successful peaceful outcomes.","Separated documented formal process from the unresolved counterfactual question of whether credible peaceful alternatives were exhausted before force."],"reasons_to_reopen_full_ledger":["Reopen if complete parliamentary and cabinet records become available for state-of-siege extensions or particular force authorizations.","Reopen if independent evidence clarifies whether Tshisekedi personally authorized or supported specific FARDC or proxy operations associated with the October ceasefire breakdown.","Reopen if implementation records establish whether the Nairobi, Luanda, cantonment, disarmament, and P-DDRCS commitments were funded, executed, and offered credible alternatives to force."]}
